Trace, implement and test: leetcode304 range sum query 2d immutable prefix sum

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
#include <algorithm>
#include <vector>
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class NumMatrix {
private:
    vector<vector<int>> _preSum;    
public:
    NumMatrix(const vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        if (matrix.empty()) return;
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        
        _preSum = vector<vector<int>>(m + 1, vector<int>(n + 1, 0));
        for (int i = 1; i <= m; i++)
        {
            for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++)
            {
                _preSum[i][j] = matrix[i - 1][j - 1] + _preSum[i - 1][j] + _preSum[i][j - 1] - _preSum[i - 1][j - 1];
            }            
        }
    }

    int sumRegion(int row1, int col1, int row2, int col2)
    {
        return _preSum[row2 + 1][col2 + 1] - _preSum[row2 + 1][col1] - _preSum[row1][col2 + 1] + _preSum[row1][col1];
    }
};

// Test
int main()
{
    vector<vector<int>> mat = {{3, 0, 1, 4, 2}, {5, 6, 3, 2, 1}, {1, 2, 0, 1, 5}, {4, 1, 0, 1, 7}, {1, 0, 3, 0, 5}};
    auto M = new NumMatrix(mat);
    int res = M->sumRegion(2, 1, 4, 3); // return 8
    cout << res << endl;
    res = M->sumRegion(1, 1, 2, 2); // return 11
    cout << res << endl;
    res = M->sumRegion(1, 2, 2, 4); // return 12
    cout << res << endl;

    return 0;
}
